name: Laura Sordillo
abstract_title: Cognitive impairment after chemotherapy resembles impairment seen in post-anesthesia patients: implications for the nature of consciousness
abstract: Post-chemotherapy cognitive impairment, like post-anesthesia cognitive dysfunction, may affect memory, concentration, and learning, which are critical aspects of consciousness. In post-chemotherapy cognitive impairment (chemo- brain or chemo-fog), the “fog” that occurs after receiving chemotherapy treatments can often last for long periods of time, sometimes for years after chemotherapy has finished.
